as_told.title: Major Mansmann tracked down, admits supervising Jacobs

plain: After a 1964 sighting at Vandenberg Air Force Base, a photo instrumentation specialist named Bob Jacobs says the Air Force tried to erase him and someone blew up his mailbox. Jacobs tells Michels himself that "they denied there was ever a Robert Jacobs in the Air Force", and then, in another inquiry, denied he was ever at Vandenberg, though he points to his DD214, the standard US military discharge paper, and to his officer efficiency reports. He says that one night a voice on the phone recited "fireworks in your mailbox at night. Oh, what a beautiful sight. You're going down," with a curse, "and my mailbox blew up." Robert Hastings, a researcher who writes about UFOs and nuclear bases, tells the same story second hand, saying the call came as Jacobs and his wife got home from a movie. Michels repeats it on several episodes, adding that Jacobs had managed over 130 people and was removed as a government employee. Michels also says that Jacobs's superior, Major Florenze Mansmann, was later tracked down by Hastings and other researchers and admitted, in the 1990s or "a couple decades later", that Jacobs had worked under him. So the account comes from the man himself, a researcher who knew him, and the host repeating both, and they differ only in which details they keep. If true, it shows how far officials would go to silence a witness.
